steps.stdout:
archstone init — examples/showcase/api/wanderlust.openapi.yaml (openapi adapter)

Wrote 7 file(s) to <draft>, and the shipped compiler compiled them.

Candidates: 16 proposed, 3 emitted, 1 not emitted.
  ✓ wanderlust.search  [read]  POST /v1/stays/search (no resource — untyped output)
  ✓ wanderlust.stay-details  [read]  GET /v1/stays/{stayId} (no resource — untyped output)
  ✓ wanderlust.availability  [read]  GET /v1/availability (no resource — untyped output)

  Declined by you (1) — most operations in a spec are not capabilities:
    - DELETE /v1/guests/{name}/bookings — A delete function exists in the agency's system. A person declined it; nothing offers it to an AI.

What did not survive the trip — read these before committing:
  no-response-shape [operation] (3) — no usable response shape — emitted without a resource, output or response mapping
    - wanderlust.search
    - wanderlust.stay-details
    - wanderlust.availability
  failures-not-emitted [operation] (1) — error responses carry no derivable business meaning — no `failures:` emitted
    - GET /v1/stays/{stayId}: error responses declared: 404
  contract-not-recorded [operation] (3) — no probe ran — no fixture, no contract
    - wanderlust.search
    - wanderlust.stay-details
    - wanderlust.availability
  semantic-type-degraded [field] (5) — semantic type fell back to string/text
    - POST /v1/stays/search: POST /v1/stays/search/requestBody/content/application/json/schema/properties/destination: a bare `type: string` implies no richer type
    - POST /v1/stays/search: #/components/schemas/Money/properties/currency: a bare `type: string` implies no richer type
    - POST /v1/stays/search: POST /v1/stays/search/requestBody/content/application/json/schema/properties/preferences/items: a bare `type: string` implies no richer type
    - GET /v1/stays/{stayId}: GET /v1/stays/{stayId}/parameters/0: a bare `type: string` implies no richer type
    - GET /v1/availability: GET /v1/availability/parameters/0: a bare `type: string` implies no richer type
  input-property-omitted [field] (3) — an optional input the connector cannot carry was left out — the agent cannot set it
    - POST /v1/stays/search#dates: object
    - POST /v1/stays/search#travelers: object
    - POST /v1/stays/search#budget: object
  identity-ref-not-inferred [field] (2) — emitted as `identifier`; this may be a `ref:` to a resource — only you know
    - wanderlust.stay-details#stayId: if this identifies a resource another capability returns, change `type: identifier` to `ref: <Resource>`
    - wanderlust.availability#propertyId: if this identifies a resource another capability returns, change `type: identifier` to `ref: <Resource>`

What no tool could infer for you, and what to check by hand:
  - Every `description:` is the source's own words. An agent reads them to decide
    whether to call you. They are the highest-leverage thing to rewrite.
  - Every `response.map` line carries the field it came from and a real example.
    A mapping can be structurally right and semantically wrong; only you can see that.
  - An input typed `identifier` may really be a `ref:` to a resource another
    capability returns. No source construct says so — only you know.

Report also written to <draft>/INIT-REPORT.md
